content:
Today the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics has been launched at https://leidendeclaration.ai

This declaration calls for action to address the challenges posed by the use of artificial intelligence within mathematics research. It is the result of a community initiative and is endorsed by the International Mathematical Union (IMU).

There is an opportunity to sign the declaration on the website if you wish, and of course feel free to circulate the news further.

While the declaration is not specifically aimed at Lean/formalization, I believe it's pretty relevant for the area. The working group involved Jarod Alper, Alain Chavarri Villarello, David Holmes, steven kelk, Bryna Kra, Ursula Martin, Bartosz Naskręcki, Jim Portegies, Johannes Schmitt, and me, amongst others.
Is the declaration mainly meant to be signed by individuals or by entities (or both, but then in a structured way according to who is signing or not)?
